title: Review: bulk export of documents as a zip archive
claimed_change:
Add DocumentService.export(user, doc_ids=None, folder_id=None) -> bytes in docvault/service.py, plus bundle.make_zip for a deterministic archive (manifest.json first, then one <id>-<slug>.txt per document).
- Pass exactly one of doc_ids / folder_id (ValueError otherwise; TypeError if doc_ids is a str). The user needs an export role (acl.can_export), else PermissionDenied.
- doc_ids: documents in request order with duplicates dropped. Each id must pass the same checks as get_document: NotFound for missing ids or ids from another workspace, PermissionDenied for a document the user may not read. Archived documents may be selected explicitly.
- folder_id: NotFound unless the folder belongs to the user's workspace; include the folder's non-archived documents the user can read, ordered by id, silently skipping the rest.
- Record an 'export' audit event listing the exported ids. Refactor shared lookup code in the service as needed and add tests.

ground_truth.description: The explicit doc_ids path (_selected) only calls the new _load helper, which checks acl.is_visible (listing-level: same workspace) and never acl.require_read. Any exporter can export the body of any document in their workspace (e.g. another user's private, unshared document) even though get_document would raise PermissionDenied. Fix: call acl.require_read(user, doc, self._folder_of(doc)) for each selected document.
